notable.grandline.orrin.title: "Barnacle", Captain of the Cape Wreckers
dialogue.grandline.notable.orrin: Lost, are we? Dizzy from the climb? Come down to the rocks, friend. Plenty of room down on the rocks.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.ignatz: Ignatz will join your crew if you ask: talk to him and invite him aboard.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.hilde: Hilde will join your crew if you ask: talk to her and invite her aboard.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.pippa: Pippa will join your crew if you ask: talk to her and invite her aboard.
arc.grandline.recruit_hint.sefa: Sefa will join your crew if you ask: talk to her and invite her aboard.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.why: The lighthouse at the foot of Reverse Mountain has gone dark and ships are breaking on the capes. Its keeper's sister — the last person alive who has seen the end of the Grand Line — didn't send her yearly letter.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.cast.wilhe: 'Old Wick', keeper of the Twin Capes light for forty years, and sister of the Saltfire King's navigator.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.cast.orrin: 'Barnacle', captain of the cape wreckers. Lives off the ships that miss the light — and someone is paying him to keep it dark.
arc.grandline.decision.capes_plan: whether the lamp burns tonight (talk to Old Wick)
arc.grandline.site.capes_wreck: the old wreck on the north cape
arc.grandline.site.capes_rocks: the rocks below the north cape, with a false lantern
quest.grandline.capes_wreck: The Wreck on the North Cape
quest.grandline.capes_wreck.desc: The wreckers keep their haul under the old wreck on the north cape. Go and search it — Old Wick wants anything with handwriting on it.
quest.grandline.capes_letter.desc: Among the wreckers' plunder is a letter for Old Wick in her sister's hand, sealed again by the World Government. Take it to her.
quest.grandline.capes_choice.desc: Haruka asked her sister to keep the lamp dark this year; the rookies coming down the mountain need it lit. Talk to Old Wick and decide.
quest.grandline.capes_light.desc: Barnacle's wreckers will try to stop the lamp being lit. Beat 3 of them on the lighthouse stairs.
quest.grandline.capes_dark.desc: Hang a false lantern on the rocks below the north cape, so the wreckers come to you instead of a ship.
quest.grandline.capes_orrin.desc: Orrin 'Barnacle' Sabiura, captain of the cape wreckers, wants his mail sack back. Defeat him.
scene.grandline.capes_1.start.1: narrator|Every Log Pose in the four Blues points the same way now: to the Twin Capes at the foot of Reverse Mountain, where the sea runs uphill.
scene.grandline.capes_1.end.1: narrator|The Twin Capes: two arms of black rock, and between them the sea climbing a mountain in a roaring white staircase. On the western cape stands a lighthouse. Its lamp is dark.
scene.grandline.capes_1.end.2: wilhelmina|Another one. Sit, sit — you look dizzy. Everyone's dizzy after the climb. That's when the wreckers get them.
scene.grandline.capes_1.end.3: wilhelmina|Wilhelmina Lanthorn. Old Wick, if you're rude. I've kept this light for forty years and given every rookie who passed a Log Pose. Here's yours.
scene.grandline.capes_1.end.4: wilhelmina|Three nights ago someone climbed my tower and put the lamp out. Since then two ships have gone onto the north cape. Those pirates you chased off were picking the bones.
scene.grandline.capes_1.end.5: wilhelmina|And my sister's letter didn't come. Twenty-four years she's written, once a year, from wherever she is. Not this year.
scene.grandline.capes_wreck.start.1: wilhelmina|The wreckers keep their haul under the old wreck on the north cape. Go and look. Bring me anything with handwriting on it.
scene.grandline.capes_wreck.end.1: narrator|Under the wreck's tilted deck the wreckers have stacked their plunder: rope, rum, and a Marine courier's mail sack, slit open.
scene.grandline.capes_wreck.end.2: narrator|Most of the letters are soaked. One isn't. It's addressed to 'W. Lanthorn, the Lighthouse', and someone has opened it and pressed a new seal over the flap: the eagle of the World Government.
scene.grandline.capes_letter.end.1: wilhelmina|...That's her hand. Haruka. My sister.
scene.grandline.capes_letter.end.2: wilhelmina|'Wick — don't light the lamp for me this year. They know I write to you. They're watching the light to see who comes looking. Keep it dark, and I'll stay hidden. — H.'
scene.grandline.capes_letter.end.3: wilhelmina|They opened it. They READ it. And then they paid wreckers to put my lamp out so their courier could slip past in the dark.
scene.grandline.capes_letter.end.4: narrator|From the north cape, a horn: three long blasts. The wreckers' captain wants his mail sack back.
scene.grandline.capes_choice.talk.1: wilhelmina|Forty years that lamp has burned. Every crew that came down this mountain saw it. Half of them would be on the rocks without it.
scene.grandline.capes_choice.talk.2: wilhelmina|If I light it tonight, the wreckers lose their dark, the rookies come down safe — and whoever reads my sister's letters knows somebody here is still looking for her.
scene.grandline.capes_choice.talk.3: wilhelmina|If I keep it dark, as she asks... the rocks stay hungry, Barnacle keeps hunting in the dark, and Haruka stays hidden one more year.
scene.grandline.capes_choice.talk.4: wilhelmina|I've decided a thousand things alone on this rock. Not this one. You choose.
scene.grandline.choice.capes_plan.lamp: Light the lamp. The rookies need it, and nobody tells Old Wick to sit in the dark.
scene.grandline.choice.capes_plan.dark: Keep it dark, as Haruka asked. We'll deal with Barnacle without the light.
scene.grandline.capes_choice.end.lamp.1: wilhelmina|Then up the stairs with me. Barnacle's men will try to stop us. Let them try.
scene.grandline.capes_choice.end.dark.1: wilhelmina|...Then we play his game. Hang a lantern on the rocks below the north cape. He'll think it's a ship in trouble and come to pick the bones. Only it'll be you.
scene.grandline.capes_light.end.1: narrator|The last wrecker tumbles down the lighthouse stairs. Wilhelmina strikes a match, and for the first time in three nights the great lamp turns, sweeping a white blade across the sea.
scene.grandline.capes_dark.end.1: narrator|You hang the lantern on the rocks and wait. Out of the dark comes a longboat with muffled oars — and a big man standing in the bow with a gaff hook.
scene.grandline.capes_orrin.start.lamp.1: orrin|You lit it. You LIT it! Do you know what that light costs me? Every night it burns is a night I go hungry!
scene.grandline.capes_orrin.start.dark.1: orrin|A lantern on the rocks. Oldest trick on the capes — and I fell for it. Well. You'll do instead of a ship.
scene.grandline.capes_orrin.end.1: narrator|Barnacle goes down on the rocks he made a living from.
scene.grandline.capes_orrin.end.lamp.1: narrator|Barnacle goes down on the wet rocks, in the full sweep of the beam. Out on the sea, a rookie ship comes down the mountain and steers wide of the cape.
scene.grandline.capes_orrin.end.dark.1: narrator|Barnacle goes down among the rocks he made a living from. The cape is dark and silent. Somewhere out there, the Lamplighter stays hidden for another year.
scene.grandline.capes_orrin.end.dark.2: wilhelmina|...She'd better write next year. I'll forgive her if she writes.
scene.grandline.capes_2.start.1: wilhelmina|The Log Pose points to Whisky Peak. They'll throw you a party there. Drink nothing you didn't pour yourself.
scene.grandline.capes_2.start.2: wilhelmina|And if you hear of my sister — anywhere, anyhow — you come back and tell me. Promise me that.
scene.grandline.capes_2.end.1: narrator|Whisky Peak rises out of the sea like a row of cactus spines, and every spine has a lantern on it. Music drifts across the water. Someone on the pier is already waving.
recap.grandline.capes_1: Reached the Twin Capes; Old Wick gave you a Log Pose. Her lamp has been put out, and her sister's letter never came.
recap.grandline.capes_wreck: Searched the wreckers' haul under the old wreck — and found a letter to Wick, opened and resealed by the World Government.
recap.grandline.capes_letter: Read Haruka's letter with Wick: 'Don't light the lamp for me this year. They're watching it.'
recap.grandline.capes_choice.lamp: Decided to light the lamp anyway.
recap.grandline.capes_choice.dark: Decided to keep the lamp dark, as Haruka asked.
recap.grandline.capes_light: Fought up the lighthouse stairs and lit the great lamp.
recap.grandline.capes_dark: Hung a false lantern on the rocks to draw the wreckers to you.
recap.grandline.capes_orrin: Brought down Barnacle, the wrecker of the capes.
recap.grandline.capes_orrin.lamp: Brought down Barnacle in the sweep of the lamp; rookie ships come down the mountain safely again.
recap.grandline.capes_orrin.dark: Brought down Barnacle in the dark; the Lamplighter stays hidden another year.
recap.grandline.capes_2: Followed the Log Pose to Whisky Peak, with a promise to bring Old Wick news of her sister.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.bonus.lamp: Every crew that comes down the mountain safely sends something up to the lighthouse. Wick insists you take a share: 2,500 Beli.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.bonus.dark: Wick gives you something of her sister's: an old Eternal Pose set for Whisky Peak, from the year Haruka sailed. 'She'd want it used.'
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.aid.lamp: The lighthouse beam sweeps the rocks. Barnacle has nowhere dark to hide, and you hit harder for it.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.aid.dark: Wick lends you her old night-glass. In the dark, you see Barnacle's men before they see you.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.after.wilh: The light burns or it doesn't, and either way you'll tell me if you hear of her.
Forty-one years. The light's never looked better. Mind the rocks on your way down — no, you know them now.
Dark nights are long nights. I don't mind. She's out there somewhere, safe, because we kept quiet.
arc.grandline.upward_mountain.after.town: The light's back! The rookies have stopped washing up on the north cape.
Wick's keeping the lamp dark this year. She won't say why. She just watches the sea.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.why: Whisky Peak throws a party for every crew that comes down the mountain and robs it at midnight. The town is a front for the Gilded Ledger, a criminal company — and its bookkeeper has just found an entry he can't live with.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.cast.hugo: Grandmaster of the Hunters' Lodge. The honest bounty hunters of Whisky Peak answer to him, and he's tired of sharing a town with thieves.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.cast.ignatz: 'Abacus', the Ledger's bookkeeper. Can balance any account except his conscience.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.cast.doublo: Mr. Doubloon, the Ledger's agent at Whisky Peak: a gunslinger with gold teeth and a coin for every lie.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.cast.farthi: Miss Farthing, his partner: two blades, one smile, no mercy.
arc.grandline.decision.whisky_plan: what becomes of the Ledger's books (talk to Ignatz)
arc.grandline.site.whisky_party: the party in Whisky Peak's square
arc.grandline.site.whisky_alley: the alley behind the Ledger's counting house
quest.grandline.whisky_party.desc: At midnight the music stops and the party's hosts reach for their weapons. Survive 6 of them.
quest.grandline.whisky_ignatz.desc: Someone hissed at you from behind a wine barrel: the counting house, back door, bring the bounty hunter. Talk to Ignatz Sorobanji.
quest.grandline.whisky_hunt.desc: The Ledger has noticed its books are missing. Beat 3 of the enforcers sent to silence Ignatz.
quest.grandline.whisky_choice.desc: Ignatz holds the Gilded Ledger's books. Hugo wants them for the Lodge; Ignatz would rather the Ledger thought they burned. Talk to Ignatz and decide.
quest.grandline.whisky_lodge.desc: Put the Ledger's books in Hugo's hands at the Hunters' Lodge.
quest.grandline.whisky_copy.desc: Keep the counting-house door while Ignatz copies the books: beat 3 of Doubloon's guards there.
scene.grandline.whisky_1.end.1: narrator|Whisky Peak greets you with fireworks, a brass band and a banner: WELCOME, HEROES OF THE SEA! Everyone is smiling. Everyone is smiling slightly too much.
scene.grandline.whisky_1.end.2: hugo|Sit at my bar, rookie, and keep your back to the wall. Hugo Kariudo, Grandmaster of the Hunters' Lodge. The honest hunters in this town drink here. The rest of them... work the party.
scene.grandline.whisky_1.end.3: hugo|At midnight, the 'hosts' rob every crew that came in tonight. It's been that way for two years, ever since a company called the Gilded Ledger bought the town hall.
scene.grandline.whisky_1.end.4: hugo|I can't touch them — they've bought the mayor and half my hunters. You, though, are a guest. Guests may defend themselves.
scene.grandline.whisky_party.start.1: narrator|Midnight. The music stops in the middle of a bar. Every smiling host in the square puts down a glass and picks up a weapon.
scene.grandline.whisky_party.end.1: narrator|The last 'host' goes down in a heap of party streamers. In the sudden quiet, someone is hissing at you from behind a barrel of wine.
scene.grandline.whisky_party.end.2: ignatz|Psst. Not here. The counting house. Back door. Bring the bounty hunter.
scene.grandline.whisky_ignatz.end.1: ignatz|Ignatz Sorobanji. I keep the Gilded Ledger's books. Kept. I'm resigning. Effective tonight. Please don't shoot me.
scene.grandline.whisky_ignatz.end.2: ignatz|Two years of robbing party guests — fine, that's just theft. But last month a new column appeared. 'Desert contract: salt delivered to wells, per oasis.' Signed by the President. Code-name Mr. Crown.
scene.grandline.whisky_ignatz.end.4: ignatz|Alabasta's. A whole kingdom. They're poisoning the water so the king has to buy it from them. I can add, you see. I know what that column means.
scene.grandline.whisky_ignatz.end.5: ignatz|And now Mr. Doubloon has noticed the books are missing. He'll have sent his enforcers already.
scene.grandline.whisky_hunt.end.1: narrator|The enforcers go down in the alley behind the counting house. One of them carries a coin stamped with a crown, and a list of names. Ignatz's is at the top.
scene.grandline.whisky_hunt.end.2: ignatz|...Ah. I'd hoped to be second at least.
scene.grandline.whisky_choice.talk.1: ignatz|I have the books. Now what? Doubloon and Farthing will come for them tonight, and I'd like to still be alive tomorrow, if it can be arranged.
scene.grandline.whisky_choice.talk.2: hugo|Give them to the Lodge. I'll copy every page to every hunter between here and the Red Line. By next week every Ledger agent has a price on their head — and my hunters will stand with you tonight.
scene.grandline.whisky_choice.talk.3: ignatz|And by next week Mr. Crown knows exactly what we know, and moves faster in Alabasta. Or — we let them think the books burned. I copy the pages that matter. We carry them to Alabasta ourselves, and nobody sees us coming.
scene.grandline.whisky_choice.talk.4: hugo|Then my hunters stay out of it, and you two face the coin-names alone tonight.
scene.grandline.whisky_choice.talk.5: ignatz|I'm told I'm worth the risk. I'd like to believe it. You decide; you're holding the lantern.
scene.grandline.choice.whisky_plan.lodge: Give the books to Hugo's Lodge. Every honest hunter should read them.
scene.grandline.choice.whisky_plan.copy: Let the Ledger think the books burned. Ignatz copies what matters, and we carry it to Alabasta.
hugo|Then come to the Lodge. I want the books in my hands before the bell, and my hunters on the doors.
scene.grandline.whisky_choice.end.copy.1: ignatz|The counting house, then. Doubloon's men guard it at night — they think the books are still inside. Keep them busy and I'll copy. I'm very fast. Terrified people usually are.
scene.grandline.whisky_lodge.end.1: narrator|At the Lodge, Hugo opens the ledger on the bar and every hunter in the room goes silent. Then, one by one, they check their guns.
scene.grandline.whisky_copy.end.1: narrator|In the counting house, Ignatz copies by candlelight while you keep the door. When he's done he sets the original books in the stove, very gently, as if apologising to them.
scene.grandline.whisky_2.start.1: doubloon|You've been drinking our wine and breaking our hosts. That goes on the bill.
scene.grandline.whisky_2.start.lodge.1: doubloon|The LODGE has our books? Then we burn the Lodge. Farthing!
scene.grandline.whisky_2.start.copy.1: doubloon|Our books are ash. Shame. The bookkeeper will have to do instead. Farthing — the rookie first.
scene.grandline.whisky_2.end.1: narrator|Mr. Doubloon and Miss Farthing go down under the WELCOME banner. Whisky Peak's parties are just parties again.
scene.grandline.whisky_2.end.lodge.1: narrator|Mr. Doubloon and Miss Farthing go down in the square under the WELCOME banner. Hugo's hunters have them in irons before they hit the ground.
scene.grandline.whisky_2.end.lodge.2: hugo|By morning there'll be a poster for every coin-name in the Ledger. Good hunting, rookie.
scene.grandline.whisky_2.end.copy.1: narrator|Mr. Doubloon and Miss Farthing go down in the square under the WELCOME banner. As far as the Gilded Ledger knows, its books burned with them.
scene.grandline.whisky_2.end.copy.2: ignatz|Nobody knows what we know. I've never been so frightened or so pleased.
scene.grandline.recruit_ignatz.start.1: narrator|Ignatz is sitting on his packed bag at the edge of the square, doing sums in a notebook to calm himself down.
scene.grandline.recruit_ignatz.end.1: ignatz|Every crew needs someone who can count. Ask me, and I'll sail.
scene.grandline.recruit_ignatz.end.2: ignatz|The Log Pose points to Little Garden next.
scene.grandline.recruit_ignatz.end.lodge: ignatz|I'll be the most wanted bookkeeper in the Grand Line by next week. Which is a bit thrilling, actually.
ignatz|Every crew needs someone who can count — the food, the powder, the Beli. You'd be amazed what disappears when nobody counts.
ignatz|I'm a quartermaster. Ask me, and I'll sail. And I'd like to see Alabasta's wells run clear; I helped with the sums that salted them.
ignatz|The Log Pose points to Little Garden next. A prehistoric island. I've budgeted for dinosaurs.
ignatz|The copies are sewn into the lining of my coat. If Mr. Crown ever finds out, I'm a dead man. So I'd prefer to be a dead man somewhere with good company.
ignatz|Every crew needs someone who can count — the food, the powder, the Beli. You'd be amazed what disappears when nobody counts.
ignatz|I'm a quartermaster. Ask me, and I'll sail — and when we reach Alabasta, these pages will do the talking.
ignatz|The Log Pose points to Little Garden next. A prehistoric island. I've budgeted for dinosaurs.
recap.grandline.whisky_1: Reached Whisky Peak's party and met Hugo of the Hunters' Lodge: the town robs its guests at midnight.
recap.grandline.whisky_ignatz: Met Ignatz, the Gilded Ledger's bookkeeper: the company is salting Alabasta's wells for a 'Mr. Crown'.
recap.grandline.whisky_hunt: Broke the enforcers sent to silence Ignatz.
recap.grandline.whisky_choice.lodge: Decided to give the Ledger's books to Hugo's Lodge.
recap.grandline.whisky_choice.copy: Decided to let the Ledger think its books burned, and carry copies to Alabasta.
recap.grandline.whisky_lodge: Put the books in Hugo's hands; the Lodge's hunters armed themselves.
recap.grandline.whisky_copy: Held the counting-house door while Ignatz copied the books and burned the originals.
recap.grandline.whisky_2: Brought down Mr. Doubloon and Miss Farthing.
recap.grandline.whisky_2.lodge: Brought down Mr. Doubloon and Miss Farthing with the Lodge's hunters beside you; every Ledger agent will soon have a price on their head.
recap.grandline.whisky_2.copy: Brought down Mr. Doubloon and Miss Farthing; the Ledger believes its books burned.
recap.grandline.recruit_ignatz: Ignatz will be your quartermaster if you ask. The Log Pose points to Little Garden.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.bonus.lodge: The Lodge makes you an honorary hunter: two pairs of seastone cuffs, and the respect of every bounty hunter in Paradise.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.bonus.copy: Ignatz 'reallocates' the Ledger's petty cash to you: 5,000 Beli. 'Consider it severance pay.'
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.aid.lodge: Hugo's hunters hold the edges of the square. Fewer blows reach you.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.after.hugo: Whisky Peak's parties are just parties again. I almost miss the excitement. Almost.
The posters went out this morning. Thirty-one coin-names, thirty-one prices. Best week the Lodge ever had.
Quiet work, the bookkeeper's way. I don't like it. I respect it.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.after.ignat: I've been counting the days since I resigned. Eleven. Eleven very good days.
arc.grandline.gilded_welcome.after.towns: Free drinks for whoever closed down the midnight robberies! That's you? Free drinks!
The Lodge has a whole wall of Ledger posters now. People come from three islands to look at it.
They say the Ledger's books burned. Shame. Probably.
arc.grandline.bake_off.why: On prehistoric Little Garden two giant grandmothers have cooked against each other for seventy years: whoever's dish makes the other cry wins. Nobody has cried yet. Now someone is raiding their pantries, and a Ledger agent wants the island quiet.
arc.grandline.bake_off.cast.astrid: giant grandmother, seventy years into a cooking duel. Proud, loud and very good with a ladle.
arc.grandline.bake_off.cast.ylva: the other giant grandmother. Insists she would raid Astrid's pantry to her face.
arc.grandline.bake_off.cast.hilde: 'Little' Hilde, Astrid's granddaughter — little for a giant — and the best cook on the island.
arc.grandline.bake_off.cast.shilling: Mr. Shilling of the Gilded Ledger: the Wax-Wax Fruit, a white suit, and a plan to make the island very quiet.
arc.grandline.decision.garden_plan: how the final tasting goes (talk to Hilde)
arc.grandline.site.garden_pantry: the raiders' camp by Hilde's kitchen
arc.grandline.site.garden_duel_ground: the ferns around the duel ground
quest.grandline.garden_ylva.desc: Astrid says Ylva raided her pantry. Ylva will say she didn't. Talk to Ylva — and taste whatever she's cooking.
quest.grandline.garden_pantry.desc: Both giants' pantries have been raided by small people who leave wax on everything. Beat 5 of the raiders camped by Little Hilde's kitchen.
quest.grandline.garden_hilde.desc: Hilde has seen the man in the white suit measuring the grandmothers at night. Talk to her.
quest.grandline.garden_choice.desc: Mr. Shilling will strike during tonight's tasting. Hilde has a dangerous idea; Astrid would rather keep tradition. Talk to Hilde and decide.
quest.grandline.garden_dish.desc: Serve Hilde's dish to both grandmothers at once: talk to Astrid and to Ylva.
quest.grandline.garden_guard.desc: Shilling's men are hiding in the ferns around the duel ground. Beat 3 of them before the tasting begins.
scene.grandline.garden_1.end.1: narrator|Little Garden: ferns taller than houses, a smoking volcano, and somewhere in the jungle a sound like two cathedrals arguing.
scene.grandline.garden_1.end.2: astrid|A visitor! A tiny one! Sit, sit — no, not on that, that's a spoon. Astrid Kamameshi. You've arrived on day twenty-five thousand, six hundred and twelve of the Bake-Off.
scene.grandline.garden_1.end.3: astrid|Seventy years Ylva and I have cooked against each other. Whoever's dish makes the other cry wins. Nobody has cried. We are both extremely good.
scene.grandline.garden_1.end.4: astrid|But someone's been raiding my pantry. Ylva says it isn't her. Ylva would say that. Go and ask her — and taste whatever she's making. Tell me if it's better than mine. It isn't.
scene.grandline.garden_ylva.end.1: ylva|Raiding Astrid's pantry? I'd never. I'd raid it to her FACE. ...Taste this. Honestly. Is it good? It's good. Is it better than hers? Don't answer that.
scene.grandline.garden_ylva.end.2: ylva|Someone's been in MY pantry too. Small people. Pirate people. They leave candle-wax on everything. Very rude.
scene.grandline.garden_ylva.end.3: ylva|They camp by the young one's kitchen — Little Hilde, Astrid's granddaughter. Hilde's the best cook on this island, and if you tell either of us I said so, I'll deny it.
scene.grandline.garden_pantry.end.1: narrator|The raiders' sacks hold giants' flour by the barrel — and bundles of fat white candles, each stamped with a little coin.
scene.grandline.garden_pantry.end.2: hilde|Coin candles. I've seen those. A man in a wax-white suit has been walking the duel ground at night, measuring the grandmothers with a tape.
scene.grandline.garden_hilde.end.1: hilde|I'm Hilde. Little Hilde. Little for a giant, which is still bigger than your house. Sorry.
scene.grandline.garden_hilde.end.2: hilde|The man in white is called Mr. Shilling. I heard him with the raiders. Tonight's the final tasting of the year, and while Grandma and Ylva are tasting, he'll seal them both in wax. Like statues.
scene.grandline.garden_hilde.end.3: hilde|He wants the island quiet. No giants, no duel, just a hidden harbour for his company's ships. And the grandmothers will be standing in the middle of the duel ground with their eyes shut, tasting.
scene.grandline.garden_choice.talk.1: hilde|I have an idea. A bad one, maybe. What if I cook a third dish — mine — and serve it to both of them at once?
scene.grandline.garden_choice.talk.2: hilde|If it makes them both cry, they both lose. The duel's over. Seventy years, done. And they won't be standing still with their eyes shut when Shilling comes. They'll be hugging. Or shouting. Probably both.
scene.grandline.garden_choice.talk.3: astrid|End the Bake-Off? My life's work? With a — with a THIRD DISH?
scene.grandline.garden_choice.talk.4: hilde|Or we do it Grandma's way: the tasting goes on, and you guard them while they taste. The duel goes on another seventy years. They'd like that. ...And I'd still be here, cooking for two people who never finish.
scene.grandline.garden_choice.talk.5: astrid|Don't look at me, tiny one. I'm too proud to choose and too old to be talked out of anything. You decide.
scene.grandline.choice.garden_plan.third: Hilde cooks a third dish. End the duel — let both grandmothers cry.
scene.grandline.choice.garden_plan.guard: Let the tasting go on. Guard the grandmothers while they taste.
scene.grandline.garden_choice.end.third_: hilde|Then I need your help serving. Grandma and Ylva, at exactly the same moment, or they'll never forgive me.
astrid|Good! Tradition! Shilling's men will be in the ferns around the duel ground. Clear them out before we sit down.
scene.grandline.garden_dish.end.1: narrator|Astrid tastes. Ylva tastes. There is a long silence on the duel ground.
scene.grandline.garden_dish.end.2: narrator|Then two giant grandmothers burst into tears at exactly the same moment, and the sound is like two cathedrals falling in love.
scene.grandline.garden_dish.end.3: ylva|Seventy years! SEVENTY YEARS, and the CHILD —
scene.grandline.garden_dish.end.4: astrid|— the child beats us BOTH —
scene.grandline.garden_guard.end.1: narrator|The last of Shilling's men flees through the ferns. On the duel ground the grandmothers sit down to the final tasting of the year, eyes closed, perfectly still.
scene.grandline.garden_2.start.1: shilling|A quiet island is a profitable island. Hold still.
scene.grandline.garden_2.start.third_dis: shilling|Weeping giants! Moving giants! This is not how wax works!
narrator|Mr. Shilling stands in the middle of the duel ground with his hands dripping white, and two crying grandmothers turn to look at him.
scene.grandline.garden_2.start.guard.1: shilling|Eyes closed, sitting still... perfect. Just a little wax —
scene.grandline.garden_2.start.guard.2: narrator|— and you are standing between him and the grandmothers.
scene.grandline.garden_2.end.1: narrator|Mr. Shilling goes down in a puddle of his own wax. Little Garden is loud again.
narrator|Mr. Shilling goes down in a puddle of his own wax. Two giant grandmothers pick him up between them and throw him a very long way out to sea.
astrid|We'll cook together now. Badly, I expect. We've never had to agree on salt.
scene.grandline.garden_2.end.guard.1: narrator|Mr. Shilling goes down at the edge of the duel ground. Behind you, the grandmothers open their eyes, taste, and declare — for the twenty-five thousandth time — a draw.
scene.grandline.recruit_hilde.start.1: narrator|Hilde is packing a knife roll the size of a canoe, and pretending not to look at your ship.
scene.grandline.recruit_hilde.end.1: hilde|I'm a cook. Ask me to come.
scene.grandline.recruit_hilde.end.2: hilde|The Log Pose points to Drum Island. Pack a coat.
scene.grandline.recruit_hilde.end.third_: hilde|They both cried. Because of my cooking. I'm going to remember that until I'm older than they are.
hilde|And now they don't need me to cook for them — they've got each other to argue with. I want to taste the whole world. Every sea, every kitchen.
hilde|I'm a cook. A big one. Ask me to come, and I'll feed your whole crew till they burst.
astrid|Take her, tiny one. And bring her back to visit, or I'll come and find you.
hilde|The Log Pose points to Drum Island next — snow, and a mountain shaped like a drum. Pack a coat.
hilde|The duel goes on. They're happy. They'll be happy for seventy more years, and I'll be... still cooking for two people who never finish.
hilde|I want to taste the whole world. Every sea, every kitchen. Grandma says go. She said it while tasting, with her eyes closed, which is how I know she meant it.
hilde|I'm a cook. A big one. Ask me to come, and I'll feed your whole crew till they burst.
ylva|Go on, little one. We'll keep the duel warm for you.
hilde|The Log Pose points to Drum Island next — snow, and a mountain shaped like a drum. Pack a coat.
recap.grandline.garden_1: Reached Little Garden on day 25,612 of the giants' Bake-Off; Astrid's pantry has been raided.
recap.grandline.garden_ylva: Tasted Ylva's dish; her pantry has been raided too, by small people who leave wax on everything.
recap.grandline.garden_pantry: Caught the pantry raiders: their candles carry the Gilded Ledger's coin.
recap.grandline.garden_hilde: Little Hilde overheard Mr. Shilling's plan: seal both grandmothers in wax during the final tasting.
recap.grandline.garden_choice.third_dish: Decided Hilde should cook a third dish to end the duel.
recap.grandline.garden_choice.guard: Decided to let the tasting go on, and guard it.
recap.grandline.garden_dish: Served Hilde's dish: both grandmothers cried at the same moment. The Bake-Off is over after seventy years.
recap.grandline.garden_guard: Cleared Shilling's men out of the ferns before the final tasting.
recap.grandline.garden_2.third_dish: Brought down Mr. Shilling; the weeping grandmothers threw him into the sea together.
recap.grandline.garden_2.guard: Brought down Mr. Shilling; the Bake-Off goes on, and another draw was declared.
recap.grandline.recruit_hilde: Little Hilde wants to taste the whole world. She'll cook for you if you ask — and the Log Pose points to Drum Island.
arc.grandline.bake_off.bonus.third_dish: The grandmothers cook their first meal together and send you away with a giant's portion: eight Sea King steaks.
arc.grandline.bake_off.bonus.guard: Astrid and Ylva agree on one thing: you're welcome on Little Garden forever. They pay you 4,000 Beli and enough meat to sink a rowboat.
arc.grandline.bake_off.aid.third_dish: Hilde's dish is still warm in your stomach. Your wounds close as you fight.
arc.grandline.bake_off.aid.guard: Two giant grandmothers sit behind you with their eyes closed. You'd rather fall than let Shilling past, and you take his blows like it.
arc.grandline.bake_off.after.astrid: Little Garden is loud again. Good. Quiet islands make me nervous.
arc.grandline.bake_off.after.astrid.thir: Ylva and I cooked together today. It was terrible. We laughed for an hour.
arc.grandline.bake_off.after.astrid.guar: Day twenty-five thousand seven hundred! Still a draw! Sit, sit, taste.
arc.grandline.bake_off.after.ylva: Taste this. Is it better than hers? Don't answer that.
arc.grandline.bake_off.after.ylva.third_: Did you know Astrid salts her soup TWICE? Seventy years and I never knew. We're having words about it.
arc.grandline.bake_off.after.ylva.guard: Same again tomorrow. It's always same again tomorrow, and I wouldn't change it.
arc.grandline.bake_off.after.hilde: The knife roll's packed. It's been packed for days. Hint.
arc.grandline.panacea.why: Drum Island is hooked on 'Panacea Tonic', sold from the castle on the drum-shaped mountain. It keeps the kingdom just sick enough to keep buying — and the one doctor who said so was run out of town.
arc.grandline.panacea.cast.pippa: Dr. Pippa Frostwhistle of the Long-Arm Tribe, the island's real doctor — run out of town for saying the tonic was poison.
arc.grandline.panacea.cast.raven: 'Stormcrow', a rival Supernova with the Smoke-Smoke Fruit and no patience at all.
arc.grandline.panacea.cast.panacea: 'Doctor' Quentin Panacea, the quack in the castle. Sells a cure for everything that cures nothing.
arc.grandline.decision.drum_plan: how to take the castle (talk to Pippa)
arc.grandline.site.drum_peddlers: the tonic peddlers in the village
quest.grandline.drum_rounds.desc: Pippa still does her rounds — at night, through windows. Go with her: talk to 2 of her patients.
quest.grandline.drum_raven.desc: A rival rookie in a feathered cloak has been testing the tonic. Talk to Raven Arashi.
quest.grandline.drum_peddlers.desc: Panacea's peddlers sell his tonic door to door. Break 4 of them.
quest.grandline.drum_choice.desc: Raven wants to smoke the quack out; Pippa wants the real medicine safe first. Talk to Pippa and decide.
quest.grandline.drum_smoke.desc: Meet Raven at the castle gate and let her fill it with smoke.
quest.grandline.drum_cure.desc: Climb in the back way and take the castle's medicine stores: beat 3 of the guards there.
scene.grandline.drum_1.end.1: narrator|Drum Island: snow on everything, and a mountain shaped exactly like a drum with a castle balanced on top. In every window of the village, a little brown bottle: PANACEA TONIC.
scene.grandline.drum_1.end.2: pippa|Don't drink that. Whatever they offered you. Put it down. Pippa Frostwhistle — doctor. The real kind, with a licence, and long arms, as you've noticed.
scene.grandline.drum_1.end.3: pippa|Doctor Panacea up in the castle sells that tonic as a cure for everything. It cures nothing. It keeps you feeling just ill enough to buy another bottle. I said so in the square, and they ran me out of town.
scene.grandline.drum_1.end.4: pippa|I still do my rounds. At night. Through windows. Come with me and you'll see.
scene.grandline.drum_rounds.end.1: resident|Doctor Frostwhistle? At my window? ...My son's been on the tonic for a year. He's worse. He's always a little worse.
scene.grandline.drum_rounds.end.2: pippa|Of course he is. Thank you. Don't give him another drop — I'll bring something real. ...If I can get it. Panacea bought up every herb on the island.
scene.grandline.drum_rounds.end.3: narrator|On the way back, a figure in a feathered cloak drops out of a snow-laden pine in front of you, trailing smoke.
scene.grandline.drum_raven.end.1: raven|Raven Arashi. Supernova. Stormwing. You've heard of me. ...You haven't? You will.
scene.grandline.drum_raven.end.2: raven|I came for a cure for my navigator's cough and got a bottle of nonsense. So I had the nonsense tested. Sugar, ice-spirit, and a little slow poison.
scene.grandline.drum_raven.end.3: raven|That quack is getting rich keeping a whole kingdom sick. I'm going to fill his castle with smoke until he comes out coughing. Want to watch?
scene.grandline.drum_raven.end.4: pippa|He'll burn the medicine stores if you smoke him out. Every real herb on this island is up in that castle.
scene.grandline.drum_peddlers.end.1: narrator|The tonic peddlers go down in the snow, bottles smashing pink. One carries an order sheet from the castle: DOUBLE THE DOSE BEFORE WINTER. RAISE THE PRICE.
scene.grandline.drum_peddlers.end.2: pippa|Before winter. He wants them too weak to come up the mountain and complain.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.talk.1: raven|My way: I fill the castle with smoke, he runs out the front door coughing, and you knock him flat in the snow. I'll be right beside you. Quick, loud, done.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.talk.2: pippa|And when the smoke goes in, he burns the stores to spite us. Every herb, every real medicine. I'd have to start from nothing, in winter.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.talk.3: pippa|My way: we climb in the back, take the real medicine before he knows we're there, and THEN deal with him. His guards will be at the stores. It's slower. It's harder. And nobody waits a winter for a cure.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.talk.4: raven|And I don't do slow. If you go Pippa's way, I'm leaving. This island's cold.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.talk.5: pippa|Your call. You're the one he'll be swinging at.
scene.grandline.choice.drum_plan.smoke: Raven's way: smoke him out. Quick, loud, done.
scene.grandline.choice.drum_plan.cure: Pippa's way: take the real medicine first.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.end.smoke.1: raven|HA! Find me at the castle gate. Bring a scarf.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.end.cure.1: raven|Suit yourselves. Stormcrow's leaving. Try not to die of patience.
scene.grandline.drum_choice.end.cure.2: pippa|The back way is up the north face, and the stores are guarded. I'll carry the bottles; you carry the argument.
scene.grandline.drum_smoke.end.1: narrator|Raven opens her hands and the castle simply fills, every window pouring grey. Somewhere inside, glass is breaking and someone is screaming about his inventory.
scene.grandline.drum_cure.end.1: narrator|The store-room guards go down among the shelves. Pippa's long arms sweep jar after jar into her bag: real herbs, real medicine, a whole winter's worth.
scene.grandline.drum_2.start.1: panacea|A dose for everyone! Payable in advance!
scene.grandline.drum_2.start.smoke.1: panacea|*cough* My tonic! My STOCK! You've ruined a perfectly good monopoly!
scene.grandline.drum_2.start.smoke.2: raven|And you look awful. Have you tried a tonic?
scene.grandline.drum_2.start.cure.1: panacea|Where are my herbs? Who's been in my stores? The rookie and the — the LICENSED one!
scene.grandline.drum_2.end.1: narrator|Doctor Panacea goes down in the snow. Drum Island will get better now.
scene.grandline.drum_2.end.smoke.1: narrator|Doctor Panacea goes down face-first in the snow. Behind him, the castle's stores are a column of fragrant smoke rising into the sky.
scene.grandline.drum_2.end.smoke.2: pippa|...I'll start brewing tonight. From nothing. Again.
scene.grandline.drum_2.end.smoke.3: raven|Not bad, rookie. You hit like a storm. See you at Sabaody — I'll be the one with the bigger bounty.
scene.grandline.drum_2.end.cure.1: narrator|Doctor Panacea goes down in his own doorway. Down in the village Pippa's bag is already open, and the first real medicine Drum has seen in years is going from window to window.
scene.grandline.recruit_pippa.start.1: narrator|Pippa is in the village square in the snow, mixing medicine for a queue that stretches out of sight.
scene.grandline.recruit_pippa.end.1: pippa|I'm a doctor. A ship needs one more than an island does. Ask me.
scene.grandline.recruit_pippa.end.2: pippa|The Log Pose points to Alabasta.
pippa|It'll take me the whole winter to grow it all back. ...And then what? Wait for the next quack?
pippa|Out there are diseases nobody's named and cures nobody's found. There's a sickness in the New World that turns people to seastone, they say. I'd like to cure it.
pippa|I'm a doctor. A ship needs one more than an island does. Ask me.
pippa|And your Log Pose points to Alabasta. A desert kingdom. Bring water — no, really. I've heard something's wrong with their wells.
scene.grandline.recruit_pippa.end.cure.1: pippa|Every house in the village has real medicine tonight. Because of you. The town wants me to stay. They actually asked.
scene.grandline.recruit_pippa.end.cure.2: pippa|But out there are diseases nobody's named and cures nobody's found. There's a sickness in the New World that turns people to seastone, they say. I'd like to cure it.
scene.grandline.recruit_pippa.end.cure.3: pippa|I'm a doctor. A ship needs one more than an island does. Ask me.
scene.grandline.recruit_pippa.end.cure.4: pippa|And your Log Pose points to Alabasta. A desert kingdom. Bring water — no, really. I've heard something's wrong with their wells.
recap.grandline.drum_1: Reached Drum Island, hooked on Panacea Tonic, and met Dr. Pippa Frostwhistle, run out of town for telling the truth.
recap.grandline.drum_rounds: Did Pippa's night rounds: the patients on the tonic only get worse.
recap.grandline.drum_raven: Met the rookie Raven Arashi: the tonic is sugar, spirits and slow poison.
recap.grandline.drum_peddlers: Broke the tonic peddlers: Panacea means to double the dose before winter.
recap.grandline.drum_choice.smoke: Decided to let Raven smoke Panacea out.
recap.grandline.drum_choice.cure: Decided to take the real medicine before facing Panacea.
recap.grandline.drum_smoke: Raven filled the castle with smoke.
recap.grandline.drum_cure: Took the castle's real medicine from under its guards' noses.
recap.grandline.drum_2.smoke: Brought down Doctor Panacea in the snow; the castle's stores burned.
recap.grandline.drum_2.cure: Brought down Doctor Panacea; real medicine went from window to window that night.
recap.grandline.recruit_pippa: Pippa wants to cure what nobody has cured. She'll be your doctor if you ask — and the Log Pose points to Alabasta.
arc.grandline.panacea.bonus.smoke: Raven tosses you a souvenir from the castle kitchen — two smoked Sea King steaks — and pirates all over Paradise hear you stormed a castle with Stormcrow.
arc.grandline.panacea.bonus.cure: The village was cured in a night. Drum Island's shops give you 15% off from now on.
arc.grandline.panacea.aid.smoke: Raven's smoke rolls round the fight. Panacea can't see you coming, and you hit harder for it.
arc.grandline.panacea.after.pippa: The village is getting better. I'm getting restless. Those two things are related.
arc.grandline.panacea.after.raven: Rookie. Still alive? Good. I'd hate to beat a dead rival.
arc.grandline.panacea.after.raven.smoke: You hit like a storm, rookie. I'll see you at Sabaody.
arc.grandline.panacea.after.raven.cure: Patience. Ugh. Fine, it worked. Don't tell anyone I said so.
arc.grandline.panacea.after.townsfolk.dr: No more tonic. Just snow and soup. Lovely.
The castle burned, the quack's gone, and Doctor Frostwhistle's brewing day and night. We'll be all right by spring.
Real medicine! The whole village is out of bed! The shops are giving whoever brought it a winter discount — that's you.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.why: Alabasta's oases are turning to salt, and the king must buy his people's water from the Gilded Ledger. Its President is a Warlord the World Government's charter protects — and what he really wants lies under the palace.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.cast.sefa: 'the Stone-Reader', a young archaeologist who can read a little of the forbidden script.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.cast.rashid: King of Alabasta. Ate the Forest-Forest Fruit and has spent forty years greening the desert one tree at a time.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.cast.celestine: Madam Sovereign, the Ledger's vice-president: the Flower-Flower Fruit and a casino where every table is rigged.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.cast.saltmarsh: Sir Barnaby Saltmarsh, the Salt Baron: a Warlord of the Sea, President of the Gilded Ledger, and the Salt-Salt Fruit.
arc.grandline.decision.alabasta_plan: whether to hold the spring or the stone (talk to Sefa)
arc.grandline.site.alabasta_wells: the salted wells near the palace
quest.grandline.alabasta_stone.desc: King Rashid says his scholar knows what the Ledger is really after. Talk to Sefa Ishibumi in the palace library.
quest.grandline.alabasta_choice.desc: Tonight Saltmarsh salts the palace spring and breaks the vault, and you can only hold one. Talk to Sefa and decide.
quest.grandline.alabasta_spring.desc: Hold the palace spring: beat 4 of the Ledger's salters there.
quest.grandline.alabasta_vault.desc: Hold the vault beneath the palace: beat 4 of the Ledger's vault-breakers on the stairs.
scene.grandline.alabasta_1.end.1: narrator|Alabasta: an ocean of sand around a ribbon of green. In the oasis towns the wells taste of the sea, and water-sellers in gold-trimmed coats sell it back by the cup.
scene.grandline.alabasta_1.end.2: rashid|Rashid Sunabashi. King, technically. I ate the Forest-Forest Fruit as a boy and I've spent forty years greening this desert one tree at a time. Somebody is undoing my life's work one well at a time.
scene.grandline.alabasta_1.end.3: rashid|The water-sellers belong to a company called the Gilded Ledger. They've offered to sell the whole kingdom its water. Their price is my throne.
scene.grandline.alabasta_1.end.4: rashid|My scholar, Sefa, says they want more than the throne. She's in the palace library. She usually is.
scene.grandline.alabasta_stone.end.1: sefa|Sefa Ishibumi. They call me the Stone-Reader. They mean it as an insult. I take it as a job title.
scene.grandline.alabasta_stone.end.2: sefa|Under this palace is a poneglyph — a red stone covered in the old script the World Government made it a crime to read. I can read it. A little. Enough to know it matters.
scene.grandline.alabasta_stone.end.3: sefa|The Ledger's President is the Warlord Sir Barnaby Saltmarsh, the Salt Baron. A Warlord can't be arrested — the Government's charter protects him. He doesn't want the throne for the throne. He wants what's under it.
scene.grandline.alabasta_stone.end.4: sefa|His vice-president runs the casino at Rainbase. Madam Sovereign. If anyone has the company's plans, she does.
scene.grandline.alabasta_2.start.1: narrator|Rainbase: a casino shaped like a crocodile's grin, glittering in the sand. Every table is rigged and every dealer is armed.
scene.grandline.alabasta_2.end.1: narrator|Madam Sovereign goes down among her own roulette wheels in a storm of petals. Her office safe holds the Ledger's plan, written in gold ink.
scene.grandline.alabasta_2.end.2: sefa|'Phase Four: salt the palace spring. The king signs or the capital dies of thirst. Phase Five: the vault.' ...He's doing both. Tonight.
scene.grandline.alabasta_2.revolutionary: narrator|The Ledger's raiders break against the oasis towns' new militias. In a raider captain's satchel: the Ledger's plan, written in gold ink.
sefa|'Phase Four: salt the palace spring. The king signs or the capital dies of thirst. Phase Five: the vault.' ...He's doing both. Tonight.
scene.grandline.alabasta_choice.talk.1: sefa|He'll come at dusk with the Salt-Salt Fruit. If he salts the palace spring, the capital has no water by morning and Rashid signs anything. If he breaks the vault, the stone is salted to dust, and the history with it.
scene.grandline.alabasta_choice.talk.2: rashid|We can't hold both; his men are already at each gate. The spring is my people. I don't need to tell you which I'd choose.
scene.grandline.alabasta_choice.talk.3: sefa|And the stone is everyone's people — the ones who wrote it, and everyone who's been told it never happened. There is one. There will never be another.
scene.grandline.alabasta_choice.talk.4: rashid|I can green a salted spring. It'll take me ten years and half my strength, but I can. Nobody can rewrite that stone.
scene.grandline.alabasta_choice.talk.5: sefa|...And that's why he says it's your choice, not his. Go on. We'll both live with it.
scene.grandline.choice.alabasta_plan.spr: Hold the palace spring. Water first, for everyone alive today.
scene.grandline.choice.alabasta_plan.sto: Hold the vault. The stone holds a history the world tried to burn.
scene.grandline.alabasta_choice.end.spri: rashid|Then to the spring. Thank you. ...Sefa, I'm sorry.
scene.grandline.alabasta_choice.end.ston: sefa|The vault stairs are behind the throne. Thank you. Thank you.
rashid|Ten years. I've waited longer for less.
scene.grandline.alabasta_spring.end.1: narrator|The salters at the spring go down in the wet sand. The water runs clear and cold. From the direction of the vault comes a long, terrible grinding — stone turning to salt.
scene.grandline.alabasta_vault.end.1: narrator|The vault-breakers go down on the stairs. Behind you the poneglyph glows faintly red in the lamplight, whole. From the courtyard comes a hiss like the sea: the palace spring turning white.
scene.grandline.alabasta_3.start.1: saltmarsh|I am a Warlord of the Sea. The law protects me. Nothing protects you.
saltmarsh|The spring's clean and the stone is dust. Half a victory, rookie. Let me show you what the whole thing tastes like.
scene.grandline.alabasta_3.start.stone.1: saltmarsh|You saved a rock. The capital drinks brine tonight. Was it worth it?
scene.grandline.alabasta_3.civilian.star: rashid|Others will fight him. You and I have water to move. The caravans leave at dusk, and the Ledger will try to stop every one of them.
narrator|While others fight the Salt Baron, you keep the water caravans moving through the night. At dawn the news comes down the river: Saltmarsh has fallen, and every town on the river has water.
scene.grandline.alabasta_3.end.1: narrator|The Salt Baron falls. Alabasta's wells will run clear again.
scene.grandline.alabasta_3.end.spring.1: narrator|The Salt Baron falls, and the salt he made drifts away on the desert wind. Children are already filling buckets at the palace spring.
scene.grandline.alabasta_3.end.spring.2: sefa|...The stone's gone. I'll remember what I read. I'll write it down tonight, all of it, before I forget a single line.
scene.grandline.alabasta_3.end.stone.1: narrator|The Salt Baron falls. Under the palace the poneglyph waits, whole, for anyone who can read it. In the courtyard King Rashid kneels by the white spring with his hands in the salt, and something green begins, very slowly, to grow.
scene.grandline.recruit_sefa.start.1: narrator|Sefa is in the palace library with every lamp lit, writing as if the words might escape.
scene.grandline.recruit_sefa.end.1: sefa|I'm an archaeologist. Ask me, and I'll come.
scene.grandline.recruit_sefa.end.2: sefa|The Log Pose points to Jaya.
sefa|I read the stone before he broke it. Not all of it. Enough to know there are others — one on every island where something important was buried.
sefa|The Government burns history. I'd like to read it faster than they can burn it. That means a ship.
sefa|I'm an archaeologist. Ask me, and I'll come.
sefa|The Log Pose points to Jaya. A lawless town, they say — and a girl who wants to sail to the sky.
scene.grandline.recruit_sefa.end.stone.1: sefa|You saved it. You don't understand what that means yet. Neither do I — but I will, now that I can keep reading.
scene.grandline.recruit_sefa.end.stone.2: sefa|There are others — one on every island where something important was buried. The Government burns history. I'd like to read it faster than they can burn it.
scene.grandline.recruit_sefa.end.stone.3: sefa|I'm an archaeologist. Ask me, and I'll come.
scene.grandline.recruit_sefa.end.stone.4: sefa|The Log Pose points to Jaya. A lawless town, they say — and a girl who wants to sail to the sky.
recap.grandline.alabasta_1: Reached Alabasta, where the wells taste of the sea, and heard King Rashid out: the Gilded Ledger wants his throne.
recap.grandline.alabasta_stone: Met Sefa the Stone-Reader: under the palace lies a poneglyph, and the Ledger's President — the Warlord Saltmarsh — wants it.
recap.grandline.alabasta_2: Broke Madam Sovereign's hold on Rainbase and seized the Ledger's plan: the spring and the vault, tonight.
recap.grandline.alabasta_choice.spring: Decided to hold the palace spring.
recap.grandline.alabasta_choice.stone: Decided to hold the poneglyph's vault.
recap.grandline.alabasta_spring: Held the palace spring; the stone was salted to dust.
recap.grandline.alabasta_vault: Held the vault; the palace spring turned to salt.
recap.grandline.alabasta_3: Brought down Sir Barnaby Saltmarsh, the Salt Baron.
recap.grandline.alabasta_3.spring: Brought down the Salt Baron; the capital drinks clean water, and Sefa wrote down what she read before the stone was lost.
recap.grandline.alabasta_3.stone: Brought down the Salt Baron; the poneglyph survives, and King Rashid has begun to green his salted spring.
recap.grandline.recruit_sefa: Sefa wants to read history faster than the Government can burn it. She'll join if you ask — and the Log Pose points to Jaya.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.bonus.spring: The capital kept its water. Alabasta's people won't forget it, and its shops give you 15% off from now on.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.bonus.stone: Sefa makes you a rubbing of the stone you saved — the first ever taken from it — 'so it exists in two places now.'
arc.grandline.salt_wells.bonus.books: Ignatz lays the copied books on King Rashid's table: the Ledger's whole scheme, in its own hand. The kingdom pays its debt to you, 10,000 Beli, and the Marines finally have their case.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.aid.spring: Rashid's roots crack up through the sand around you, drinking the salt before it can reach you. Your wounds close.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.aid.stone: Sefa's sand rises in a wall between you and the worst of the salt.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.after.rashid: The wells are clear and the Ledger is finished. I still plant a tree every morning. Old habits.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.after.rashid.sp: Clean water in every cup in the capital. I think of the stone sometimes. Sefa thinks of it always.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.after.rashid.st: Look — the first shoots in the salted spring. Ten years, I said. It might only be nine.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.after.sefa: I've filled four notebooks since Saltmarsh fell. The fifth is for the next stone. Hint.
arc.grandline.salt_wells.after.townsfolk: The Salt Baron's gone and the wells taste of water again. Water! Imagine!
The capital never went dry, thanks to you. The shops won't charge you the foreigner's price any more.
The palace spring's salt, but the king says it'll be green again in ten years. We believe him. He's done it before.
